email_messages.subject: Q3 Customer Survey Results + Action Items for Shipments Visibility
email_messages.body:
Hi Maria, Jason,

Sharing the toplines from the Q3 customer satisfaction pulse (freight + warehousing accounts). Overall NPS improved slightly, but the recurring theme is shipment visibility during exceptions (weather holds, appointment reschedules).

Key takeaways:
- Customers want faster proactive updates when an ETA changes (even if we don’t have a final appointment yet).
- The carrier scorecard is appreciated, but clients want it summarized by lane and month.
- Several enterprise accounts asked for a single escalation email alias per region.

Proposed actions (April/May):
1) Jason: Can your team add an “Exception Update” template in the customer portal notifications (email + in-app) with placeholders for next update time?
2) Maria: Can Ops define a standard cadence for exception updates (e.g., initial notice within 60 mins, then every 4 hours until resolved) for Transportation?
3) Lisa: If you agree, I’ll draft regional escalation aliases and routing rules for approval.

If we can align this week, I’ll incorporate into the Q3 closeout deck for ELT.

Thanks,
Priya

email_messages.subject: Re: Q3 Customer Survey Results + Action Items for Shipments Visibility
email_messages.body:
Priya, Maria,

Yes—we can support the “Exception Update” template. A couple notes:

- We can push the template into the portal notifications in the next sprint (targeting Apr 26 release), assuming copy is finalized by Apr 18.
- For email, we’ll need approved language for what we can/can’t commit to when an appointment is pending (legal/compliance sensitivity around guaranteed ETAs).
- For the carrier scorecard by lane/month: we can generate a monthly PDF export for enterprise accounts as an interim step. A dashboard enhancement would land in May.

Maria: If you can confirm the Ops cadence you want for exceptions, I’ll map it to system triggers (e.g., event types for delay, tender rejected, appointment moved).

Lisa: If you already have naming conventions for aliases (e.g., west-escalations@), send them and we’ll ensure routing integrates with ServiceNow queues.

Thanks,
Jason

email_messages.subject: Budget Hold: May Travel Requests (Conferences + Customer Visits)
email_messages.body:
Hi all,

Finance is placing a temporary hold on new May travel approvals while we reconcile Q2 spend vs. forecast. This impacts conference attendance (e.g., CSCMP regional) and non-essential customer on-sites.

What I need from you by EOD Thursday:
1) A list of planned May trips (traveler, destination, purpose, estimated cost).
2) Whether the trip is revenue-protecting (customer retention/escalation) vs. optional.
3) If virtual attendance is viable (for events) or if we can combine visits.

We’re not canceling anything already ticketed; this is for new requests that haven’t been booked yet. I’ll consolidate and bring a recommendation to the CFO for exceptions.

Thanks,
Derek

—
Derek Holt
Director, FP&A
HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Inventory accuracy – Q2 variance + next steps
email_messages.body:
Hi Maria, Derek,

Sharing a quick readout on the inventory accuracy workstream.

Since March we’ve tightened our operational controls by rolling out a monthly cycle-count program across all regional warehouses (every site on the same calendar), and we’re now tracking count variance as a formal KPI in the weekly ops scorecard. Early results are encouraging: most sites are down to low single-digit variance, with the remaining exceptions tied to a few high-velocity SKUs.

Next steps this week:
- Standardize the root-cause tags (receiving vs. picking vs. slotting)
- Refresh the training module for new associates
- Confirm the threshold for escalating variances to site leadership

This is strictly an ops process/metrics change to improve accuracy (not a contract/approval workflow change), so it shouldn’t affect any redline review or customer-specific signoff paths.

Thanks,
Priya

Priya Nair
Director, Warehouse Operations
HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: RE: Inventory accuracy – Q2 variance + next steps
email_messages.body:
Priya — thank you.

Two quick questions for the QBR deck:
1) Can we confirm the “recent operational change” language is the monthly cycle counts + the new KPI on count variance (vs. anything system-related)?
2) Any concerns from Legal/Commercial about calling out this change publicly in customer materials?

Lisa is helping me finalize the narrative for two customers who have asked what we’ve changed to improve inventory accuracy.

Maria

Maria Gomez
Sr. Program Manager, Strategic Accounts
HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: RE: Inventory accuracy – Q2 variance + next steps
email_messages.body:
Maria — confirmed.

1) The recent operational change is exactly that: we implemented a monthly cycle-count program for all regional warehouses and started tracking count variance as a KPI (reported weekly and reviewed in the monthly ops business review). No WMS change is required to support the program.

2) I don’t see any Legal/Commercial sensitivity in stating this. It’s a general warehouse process/metrics initiative and does not touch contract redline review, customer approval workflows, or any pricing/terms. We’re just describing how we’re tightening inventory controls.

If helpful, you can phrase it as: “Standardized monthly cycle counts across all sites and introduced count variance KPI tracking to drive accountability and root-cause resolution.”

Priya
